brief: Doctrine rewrite of 2026-08-21: every line is about the weather; the picture is the evidence. Three lines per photograph (Al’s ruled keeps locked and counted). Bank rescues marked. PAIRING-TASTE + the swap test still bind.
linesLabel: three per image incl. locked keeps

images.seen: A dog asleep on warm patio tiles in the first low gold of a clear dawn, long shadows, lush garden behind, pale blue sky.
images.note: 1 line(s) already kept by Al, locked below
lines: The sun cleared the roof about ten minutes ago and the tiles are already warm.
Nothing in the sky to slow the sun down, so the stoep warmed up before seven.
alreadyKept: He will move twice before lunch and both times by about a metre.

images.seen: A wide empty beach, two wooden chairs and a cooler box under one striped umbrella, flat teal sea, huge blue sky with two thin wisps. Sunday.
lines: The sea has gone the colour it only goes when the sky is this empty.
Sunday, and the sky has cleared its whole diary for this.
Beach or braai? Yes.

images.seen: Farm dusk, orange-to-blue gradient with the first star out, fire pit lit, two kids playing soccer on the lawn. Saturday.
images.note: 2 line(s) already kept by Al, locked below
lines: The first star is out before the last of the sunset has even left.
alreadyKept: That fire was lit before anybody needed it, which is what a clear evening does.
Saturday, and the sky went from orange to blue without one cloud interrupting.

images.seen: Karoo farmyard at night, people lying on a bakkie bed pointing up at a huge Milky Way over white farm buildings.
images.note: 2 line(s) already kept by Al, locked below
lines: Perfect night to actually see the Milky Way.
alreadyKept: You have to drive two hours from anywhere to get a sky like that.
Saturday night, and the entertainment is free and about four billion years old.

images.seen: A city skyline at night from a rooftop, thousands of lights below, stars and a few small clouds above. Wednesday.
images.note: 1 line(s) already kept by Al, locked below
lines: Ten thousand streetlights down there and the sky is still winning tonight.
Tomorrow's weather is tomorrow's problem.

images.seen: Three school kids with backpacks walking down a suburban pavement in low golden dawn light, long shadows, a sunlit koppie behind, clean pale sky. Tuesday.
images.note: 1 line(s) already kept by Al, locked below
lines: Not a breath of haze this morning; even the mountain got up early.
This light lasts about twenty minutes and the walk to school gets all of it.
alreadyKept: Somewhere an estate agent is saying 'lifestyle'.

images.seen: A surfer at the water's edge at sunrise, mirror-wet sand reflecting a pastel sky, mist on the far headlands, sea completely calm. Saturday.
lines: Not enough wind this morning to put one wrinkle on that water.
The beach is doubling as a mirror, which takes one morning of absolutely no wind.
One sunrise, used twice — once in the sky and once off the wet sand.

images.seen: Friends on a city rooftop on towels with a thermos and sunscreen, Joburg skyline with the Absa building behind them, deep blue cloudless sky, hard sun. Tuesday.
images.note: 1 line(s) already kept by Al, locked below
lines: Joburg does about three hundred of these a year. Nobody is complaining.
The sky has gone that deep blue you only get this high above sea level.
alreadyKept: Days like this should come with a soundtrack.

images.seen: A dad flat on his back on the lawn with two kids piled on him laughing, jacaranda in full bloom overhead, purple flowers scattered on the grass, deep blue cloudless sky. Sunday.
images.note: 1 line(s) already kept by Al, locked below
lines: Jacarandas only do this three weeks a year, and the sky decided to match.
Grass warm, sky empty — the kind of Sunday that resets a whole family.

images.seen: A dad smirking in a deckchair with a beer and a magazine while his son pushes a reel mower over a half-brown lawn, jacaranda petals on the paving, hard midday sun, red-brick house. Saturday.
images.note: 1 line(s) already kept by Al, locked below
lines: That lawn stopped asking the sky for rain somewhere around the start of November.
The sun has done more to that lawn this month than any mower ever will.
alreadyKept: If you're working today, we feel sorry for you.

images.seen: Office workers pushing out through a glass tower's revolving door at four on a Friday, one with both arms up, the whole facade reflecting a deep blue sky, street clock reading just past four.
images.note: 1 line(s) already kept by Al, locked below
lines: Forty floors of glass and every one of them is showing the same blue.
The afternoon held exactly like the morning promised, which almost never happens.
alreadyKept: Whoever booked the four o'clock meeting is going to be sitting in it alone.

images.seen: A hadeda standing on a browned lawn next to an oscillating sprinkler mid-spray, brick house behind, deep clean blue sky. Tuesday.
lines: The only rain this garden has seen all month comes out of a pipe.
Weeks of nothing but blue, and even the hadeda has to queue at the sprinkler.
The sun has had this lawn to itself for a month and it is winning.

images.seen: Poolside table with an iced tea, sunglasses and a straw hat on the lounger, turquoise pool, aloes along the wall, deep blue gradient sky. Friday.
images.note: 1 line(s) already kept by Al, locked below
lines: The sky checked in at seven, went nowhere all day, and is staying for the weekend.
The pool is that blue because the sky is doing all of it.
alreadyKept: Bottle this one. Open it in winter.

images.seen: Two swimmers in wetsuits with towels sitting on a tidal-pool wall at sunset, flat sea, mountain silhouette behind, apricot sky with a few small clouds. Sunday.
lines: Flat sea, spent sun, and air still warm enough to sit around in a wet wetsuit.
The wind that usually owns this coast has taken the evening off.
That sky is doing its whole show over a sea too flat to interrupt it.

images.seen: Street cricket in a Karoo dorp at dusk, bin for a wicket, windpomp silhouetted against an orange-to-purple gradient, one planet out, grandparents watching from a fence. Friday.
lines: Cricket till the light goes, and light like this takes its time going.
One planet up, no clouds coming, and the whole dorp still outside.
The Karoo cools fast under a clear sky, but nobody has noticed yet.

images.seen: A man mowing his lawn in the last golden light at a modern concrete house, sun starring through a small tree, long shadows, clear pale sky. Thursday.
lines: This is the first hour since breakfast that lawn work has been survivable.
A clear evening pays out about forty minutes of gold, and it has just started.
Not a leaf moving — the day is closing as calm as it opened.

images.seen: A teenager railing a mountain-bike berm on a dirt trail at sunset, golden dust hanging in the air behind him, hills to the horizon, clear gradient sky. Wednesday.
lines: That dust is hanging in the air because there is no wind to take it anywhere.
You can see three ridgelines from here, which is what no-haze evenings are for.
The sun is at the exact height where the whole veld goes gold.

images.seen: Two birds silhouetted on a wire against a spectacular pink-and-orange cirrus sunset, bushveld dirt road and thorn trees below. Monday.
lines: Cirrus this pink means the sky is completely dry all the way up.
A sunset like this pulls an audience, and tonight it is two birds on a wire.
Monday got the best sky of the week and is wasting it on a farm road.

images.seen: Three schoolboys walking home at dusk with arms over each other's shoulders, clean orange-to-navy gradient sky, streetlights just on. Tuesday.
lines: A gradient that clean means not one cloud between here and tomorrow.
Orange to navy with nothing in between — the walk home slowed down for it.
The day used up every hour of light and still had this left over.

images.seen: A mother and toddler at an open glass door pointing at the moon, the family cat sitting on the lawn under a moonlit, starry sky. Thursday.
lines: The moon is out and somebody small is hearing about it for the first time.
Not a cloud. Just you and the Southern Cross.
Clear enough that even the cat is checking the sky.

images.seen: A brass wall lantern glowing on a stucco wall at night, a big emperor moth and a cloud of insects at the light, aloes and palms in the dark garden, stars above. Monday.
lines: Warm, still and clear: every insect in the province is at this one lamp.
Windows-open weather has arrived, and word has reached the moths.
Not a breath of wind, or that lantern would be having a quieter evening.

images.seen: A backyard dinner party under strings of fairy lights, eight friends around a long wooden table, clear navy sky above the trees. Friday.
lines: A Friday night warm enough that the table walked itself outside.
Nothing up there but stars, which is how supper ends up under them.
The evening is holding at exactly the temperature nobody talks about.

images.seen: A kids' soccer team in white shirts sitting on a curb eating slap chips out of newspaper cones, low golden sun, long shadows, clear sky. Thursday.
lines: The sun stayed out for the whole match and is hanging around for the chips.
Match played, chips out, and the sky never once threatened the fixture.
The sort of afternoon that keeps a whole soccer team sitting on a curb.

images.seen: A hadeda probing a flowerbed beside agapanthus in full bloom, deep blue summer sky, lawn and trees behind. Monday.
lines: Agapanthus out, hadeda busy, sky empty: high summer is running on schedule.
The agapanthus open for exactly this kind of sky, and they got it.
Not a cloud to slow the sun, and the whole garden is making the most of it.

images.seen: A man in a Hawaiian shirt, boardshorts and slops walking into a corporate glass office lobby with a laptop bag, suits visible inside, deep blue sky reflected in the facade. Monday.
lines: The sky made the dress-code decision this morning and he just obeyed it.
A sky like that overrules HR, and everybody at reception knows it.
Summer filed its arrival notice this morning; the shirt is the paperwork.

images.seen: Two women working on laptops under a striped beach umbrella on a Joburg rooftop, Ponte and the Hillbrow Tower on the skyline, towels and a cooler box on the concrete. Wednesday.
lines: The weather moved the office to the roof and productivity can argue later.
Wednesday this warm turns every roof in Joburg into a second office.
The sun took the direct route today: straight down, no traffic.

images.seen: Two kids leaping for a tennis ball on the lawn of a white Cape Dutch farmhouse, hard bright sun, pale clear sky. Wednesday.
lines: The kind of sun that turns one tennis ball into a whole afternoon.
That farmhouse has seen a few centuries of days like this and still gets them free.
Full sun, soft lawn, and homework has officially lost its audience.

images.seen: Two women turning boerewors on a built brick braai with tongs, two men with a salad bowl behind, smoke rising into golden late sun, garden deck. Saturday.
lines: Wors on, sun low, wind nowhere: Saturday is doing everything right.
The smoke is going straight up, which is the sky's way of approving a braai.
The braai is the social calendar. Show up.

images.seen: A golden retriever flat asleep on a sunlit wooden deck, built stone braai and benches behind, pot plants, deep blue cloudless sky. Thursday.
lines: The deck reached golden-retriever temperature about an hour ago.
The sun has been on those boards since morning and the dog is doing the audit.
Thursday's forecast, as read by the dog: warm boards until further notice.

images.why: round-1 lines retired by the doctrine redo
images.seen: An older man watering his lawn at dawn under a jacaranda in full bloom, coffee mug in hand, Weber on the stoep, one dry patch on the grass, pale clear sky. Sunday.
lines: That dry patch is what a week of cloudless skies does to a lawn.
A sky this clear hands you one cool hour, and this is it.
The Weber's been waiting all week for this.
